title: I think my game is fun, and has a unique gameplay, but no one is playing it to prove me wrong
author: Chocoweb88
selftext:
Hi everyone! I recently published a game of mine on the Android Google Play Store. It's a fast-paced, sword-themed combat card game. It's currently in open beta and free to play, so I would really appreciate it if anyone could check it out and give it a try.

My goal with this game is to build a card game that has never been seen before. I know that's quite unrealistic, but personally, I feel that my gameplay loop is pretty unique, and the experience of playing it is unlike most other card games. I also genuinely have fun playing it. But yes, I understand that this is just my personal preference and that I might be blinded by my own vision. Hence, I would really appreciate more opinions and feedback from more experienced eyes.

The UI/UX and card art are still open for further polishing and development. What I really need right now is more gameplay testing to see whether it's fun to play for everyone.

Sorry if my post title sounded arrogant! All I really wish for is for someone to give my game some try. You can find my game here https://play.google.com/apps/testing/com.Chocoweb.FiveSecondsShowdown

Or go to google play store and search "5 Seconds Showdown". Cheers and have a good day!

comments.author: AsparagusOk8818
comments.body:
i watched the trailer 

  
um 

  
is this just rock-paper-scissors? like... You made rock-paper-scissors, and you believe this is a wholly unique and mind-blowing experience that has never before been seen?

replies.author: RemarkableGuidance44
replies.body: But hey, they said its good so it must be good... lol

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
Yes, the core is just rock paper scissors. But rock paper scissors can be fun too, right? 🤣

Sincerely, I tried to add more mechanics and additional effects to make the rock-paper-scissors experience more unique. But yeah I may be too blinded by my own "vision". Thanks for watching the trailer!

replies.author: Briskfall
replies.body:
... RPS can be fun if integrated as a mechanism in another system, like Pokemon's type chart or fire emblem's weapons triangle.

On its own, it's a luck "game" much like apps that serve to determine an outcome. So as a standalone game loop system, it is pretty weak because it relies on gambling.

For many gamers, the introduction of skill expression is important OR it has to be cozy OR it needs to evoke a sense of wonder (exploration). Otherwise, the loop is not much different than pulling a slot machine or a coin toss app, which really limits your audience. Sure, RPS can be fun for... grade schoolers, who are easily impressionable by well-done special effects. Barring that cohort, it'd be a tough sell.

I am not sure if building more flourish atop of a niche foundation is the play, but you do you...

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: I understand. What I did to add more skill expressions was add effects that reduce the luck elements, e.g. some cards forced opponents to not able to play certain move, some cards are rock+ paper, higher win chance but with negative debuff ability that add risks to player... but yeah these additions wont matter if the first impression for most is "its just rock paper scissors". Its always good to hear criticism, thanks for your feedback!

replies.author: Briskfall
replies.body:
That sounds better. I would also suggest to release a trailer that's not on GPlay (many users use iPhone device and it might not be accessible unless they have a Google account). I have not seen the trailer and based my comment from the above commenter. Apologies. (I tried the link but it wouldn't let me see unless I have a Google account)

If you can manage to make the first impression that de-emphasize the rock paper scissor impression/aspect, it might actually work. I'm glad that you provided more context so it's not a totally dead idea, but the presentation and trying to sell it matters.

Since it's a card game, it might work if it can reach the uno-ish audience. A party game as a category isn't bad. You need to pick your battles though.

Also, good luck to your project. Whatever directions it might take.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body:
I'd love to expand to app ios or steam as well. One challenge for me is that, the game eventually added more unique effects, debuffs, abilities, and the gameplay will become complicated. And I wanted to avoid overwhelm player at the start so I started the tutorial simple and easy juat the core RPS element, and I supposed that is where most players will stop playing.

What you said about "RPS integrated as mechanism" inspired me, because what I did is the exact opposite.  I use RPS as core system but integrated other gameplay as supports element. Not sure how it will go in the long run, but hey its all just a part of life learning journey.

replies.author: AsparagusOk8818
replies.body:
Okay, that's fine, but when you say this:

'...My goal with this game is to build a card game that has never been seen before. I know that's quite unrealistic, but personally, I feel that my gameplay loop is pretty unique, and the experience of playing it is unlike most other card games.'

...and then 'your game' is just rock-paper-scissors; it makes you sound delusional.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: You are right. But Im glad to receive some roasts  and get the wake up call! Its better than sharing my trailer posts with no criticism at all 😅 Thanks friend

comments.author: BratPit24
comments.body: Ok I tried it a bit. It's essentially rock paper scissors and about as fun as it. Not terrible not great.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Thanks! Glad its not terrible.

replies.author: BratPit24
replies.body:
Ok I have a bit more time to be more verbose. 

1. Waaaay to much text in the beginning. Unless you want to pivot to dating sim you don't need 75% of dialogues with the lady

2.i got confused and thought the game doesn't work because I tried dropping the card at the big bright marker in the middle. While you are supposed to drag it to the opposite side. 

3. The 3 different currencies you get made me think of the super bad scam games that were super popular in 2020. Think about if you really need that. If you do it's fine. Just make sure you do. 

4. Being explicitly rock paper scissors is a double edged sword. Of course the simplicity is alluring. And the additional cards as well as the card reveal at the beginning make it just about deep enough to actually try to win. But i must say there is an inherent limit to that. For example if you have long win streak it will always feel like the game is protecting you. And contrary if you have long loss streak it will always feel like the game is cheating.

In short: cute little game for a single evening. Maybe I'd play it a bit longer If I were a student and had some boring lecture to suffer through. But id probably never put more 2-3 hours of play into it in total even at my most degenerate.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Got it! Its great to know how confusing the game is from a fresh perspective. I still have a long way to go! Cheers and thanks again for your detailed feedback.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Sincerely, my friend, Flappy Bird had over 50 million downloads before it is removed. So yeah I would really loved to join the club 😂

replies.author: BeingComfortablyDumb
replies.body: I meant join the wishful thinking club xD

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Yeah I think I am already part of it. Always nice to meet new friends 😆

comments.author: Fuzzzy420
comments.body:
Played your game. 
1. Has nothing to do with the title? 
2. I didn't expect a card game, 
3. Card game is pretty generic (rock paper scissors) 
4. A lot of stuff is happening but why? Detachment
5. Generic unit names
6. Generic title design
7. The core gameloop is boring. 

What makes your game unique? 

Sorry to say that. Good luck

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Thanks for your feedback! 1 part I am curious about, the 4th part "lots of happening", is it mean its just too messy and never explain things clearly?

replies.author: Fuzzzy420
replies.body:
The game starts and you die to an op enemy, why?. You wake up and fight instantly, but why? 
Show the family massacred or whatever happens at the start. Just give us a reason to invest. 

In the first fight the game mechanic of the title is not even there.

Then you come to the girl who explains the game. Not very intuitive I might add. 

 I would turn the tutorial upside down.  If I have to be fast why do I have to drag a small card to the top of the screen? Why not something intuitive? Or at least bigger cards and nice looking cards. 
Your cards look like out of a 10 bugs boardgame. 

In the first 60 seconds you have to hook me and you don't do that with rock paper scissors and cutscenes. Start with what's special. In a perfect world you don't need the tutorial at all. 

 Put someone in front of the game who never played a game before and watch.

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: Thanks! That is pretty insightful. I will think about how to improve the tutorial.

comments.author: Comet7777
comments.body: How are you getting the word out besides a Reddit post?

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: That's the questions I am also looking for answers.  Any suggestions?

replies.author: lemming1607
replies.body: you should attempt marketing. There's lots of free resources you should be asking your ai agent that will give you definitions of the word and where to start

comments.author: Chocoweb88
comments.body: Spent 1 year on this and afraid to show it until it is ready lol. I will do my best to polish it to a stage where I can conclude it a project done, and move on to the next stage

replies.author: LoomVale_Game
replies.body: Honestly, showing it before it felt ready took a lot of pressure off for us. We started posting the rough drafts right next to the finished piece, and it turned the whole thing into sharing instead of being judged. What's the one part you'd be least scared to show today?

replies.author: Chocoweb88
replies.body: I did showed the early version a few times previously actually, but that time didnt received any feedback lol, so I just continue pressed on
